verses.1: In the time of Ahaz, son of Yotam, and Eziya, king of Judah, Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, rose up against Jerusalem. They tried to attack it, but they were unable to defeat it.
verses.2: And he reported to the house of David, “Aram has fallen upon Ephraim. His heart and that of his people have become like branches of a tree that are broken by the wind.”
verses.3: And the LORD said to Yeshua, “Go, then, and proclaim to the people. You and your brothers shall go back to the edge of the Jordan River. Go there and prepare the way for the coming of the Lord.”
verses.4: And you said to him, “Be careful! Do not fear. Do not let your heart be troubled by these evil ones who are cunning and deceitful. Choose instead the tribes of Rezin, Aram, and Ben-Ramliah.”
verses.5: For Arnam, Ephraim, and Ben-Ramliah have forbidden you to do so.
verses.6: We will go into Judah, and we will be destroyed and killed by our own people. Then, a daughter of Tabeel will become our king.
verses.7: So said Adonai Yehovah: “Do not exist, and do not be formed.”
verses.8: For the head of Aram is Damshek, and the head of Damshek is Racin. And at the age of sixty-five years, Ephraym will be taken away from the people.
verses.9: And the chief of Ephraim, Shomron, and the chief of Shomron, son of Remaliah. If you do not believe us, then you will not be able to believe us.
verses.10: And Jehovah added words to Ahaz, saying:
verses.11: I ask you of the company of your God, Jehovah. What is that steep or high place above?
verses.12: And he said, “I will not ask nor enter into Jehovah’s sanctuary.”
verses.13: And he said, “Listen, house of David! You who are few in number, people who are weak. Do not also abandon your God.”
verses.14: Therefore, my Lord will give you this beautiful woman. She will give birth to a son, and you will call him “El.”
verses.15: Hama and Dvash will eat, according to their belief, in the good times and in difficult times.
verses.16: For before the boy knows whether Moser is good or bad, he will be forced to leave the land that you have given him.
verses.17: The LORD will bring upon us, upon our people, and upon the house of our ancestors, days when the king of Assyria will not come down from heaven against Judah.
verses.18: And on that day, the Lord will bring forth the birds that are in the ends of the land of Egypt, and also the animals that are in the land of Assyria.
verses.19: And they came and rested in the hollows of the rocks, in the crevices of the trees, in all the rugged places, and in all the difficult areas.
verses.20: On that day, Adonai will destroy the walls of the city through the river. He will also destroy its gates and even the top of the hill.
verses.21: And on that day, a man will live from a donkey’s egg and two chicks.
verses.22: And there will be plenty of milk to be eaten by the sheep. And all kinds of grass will be eaten by every animal that lives near the earth.
verses.23: And on that day, every place where there were a thousand vines would be worth a thousand pieces of silver for the purpose of cultivation and for other uses.
verses.24: In times of trouble and distress, God will come, for Shamar and Shayit will be present everywhere on the earth.
verses.25: And all the mountains that are in the valley will be shaken. There will be no fear of danger or harm. They will become a place for hunting and gathering.
